order: pure-rand xoroshiro128plus(45045), uniformInt(0, 1) per pair in id order: 0 = a on the left (column A), 1 = b

pairs.why: Game B has more happening near the player: orange animals crowd the road, with yellow pickups and red hazards adding variety later on. Game A shows similar scenery but more open stretches, while B sustains a busier, more threatening sequence before the final clearing.

Game B has more cyan road pads early, orange pickups later, and rocks passing closer to the car as it visibly swerves, giving it more activity and danger. Game A has similar scenery and rock obstacles, but the car stays mostly centered and the middle stretch looks more repetitive; both end near large windmills.

Game A has cyan pickups followed by orange objects and yellow projectiles among the bats, with large bats coming very close to the car as the action builds. Game B introduces bats earlier, but its later scenes repeat similar bat formations with fewer new things happening.

Game B has repeated coin trails and robots coming very close to the player by the middle rows, giving it more frequent activity and immediate danger. Game A stays relatively sparse longer; both build toward rocks, orange rings, and groups of robots near the end.

Game B puts spikes near the robot more often and mixes wide gaps, small stepping platforms, and elevated islands, making the action look more varied and dangerous. Game A has plenty of coins and some late spike encounters, but its platforms are generally broader and flatter, with less sustained pressure.

Game A shows repeated jumps over water, orange moving platforms, and small red hazards close to the robot, keeping danger and activity going into the later scenes. Game B has similar obstacles early, but shifts to a broad flat stretch and ends sooner, with less sustained buildup.

Game A builds toward clusters of red-edged hazards close to the player, with more obstacles and glowing effects in the later scenes. Game B has similar scenery and collectible trails, but its later stretch looks clearer and less threatening, giving A a stronger sense of escalating action.

Game A shows more frequent airborne jumps across wide gaps, with spikes near the turtle and small platforms adding danger later on. Game B has coins and occasional spikes, but the turtle spends more time on broad, safe platforms and the ending looks less demanding.
